rated_messages.input_message: Notice what is triggering your urge. Have understanding and kindness for yourself for feeling this urge. It isn't easy, but can you choose to let it be there without smoking?
Think about times in the past when you have let urges pass during a stressful moment, and notice what helped make that moment easier.

When running a marathon, the hardest part is often towards the end, but many runners stick with it, knowing that the pain will pass. Learning to quit smoking is like running a marathon - if it gets hard, you may be closer to succeeding than you realize!
You spent a long time training your brain to want a cig. Now you're retraining your brain, and it's natural that this might take time.
Are you willing to let this urge pass for the sake of living a good long time with the people who matter most to you? When you have an urge, think about the people most important to you.
If you find yourself with a few minutes to spare, it can be nice to read back over old messages. It's also a chance to reply to ones that you might have forgotten about!
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.

The best way to deal with any urges from being around smokers is to get out of the situation briefly until it goes. Make an excuse, go to the toilet, go get some water, pretend you need to get some phone reception!
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
